Instrument.name: Hyper Spectral Imager
Instrument.description: The Hyper Spectral Imager (HySI), operating in the visible and near Infrared spectral region, is one of the three imaging instruments onboard Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft for mineral logical study of the Moon. HySI is designed to map entire lunar surface in 64 contiguous bands in the visible and near infrared (VNIR: 421-964 nm) with a spatial sampling of 80m. A wedge filter is employed for the spectral separation and the image is mapped on an area detector. The detector output is processed in the front-end electronics to generate the 64-band with 12-bit quantization. The key features of HySI are as follows: - Spatial sampling : 80 x 80 sq. m (from 100 km orbit) - Swath : 20 km - Spectral range : 461 - 964 nm - No. of spectral : 64 continuous bands - No. of gains : 2 each - No. of exposure : 4 setting - Quantization : 12-bits - Signal to noise ratio > 100 - Square wave response > 40 This instrument is from Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad, India. Science Objective - Systematic topographic mapping of the entire lunar surface, including far and the polar regions - Preparation of a three-dimensional atlas of the Moon with high spatial and altitude sampling for scientific studies. The high resolution imagery of the entire moon will help detailed study of specific lunar regions of scientific interests and further our understanding of lunar evolution. There are 2 different gain settings and 4 different exposure setting of the instrument. In flight yaw mode forward describes 0 degree rotated from nominal reverse describes 180 degree rotated from nominal There are four possible orbit limb and flight yaw mode combinations: 1. descending and forward, no changes in lines or samples are performed 2. descending and reverse, samples are reversed 3. ascending and forward, both lines and samples are reversed 4. ascending and reverse. lines are reversed Refer spacecraft yaw direction and orbit limb direction keywords.
